test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which institution was established in 1921 as a deliberative body for princes?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Chamber of Princes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chamber of Princes** was established in the year **1921** as a **deliberative and advisory body** for the princely states in British India.
 
• It was set up by the British Government to provide a platform for the princely rulers to **discuss and deliberate matters** related to their states and their relationship with the British Crown.
 
• The Chamber of Princes was inaugurated by the then **Duke of Connaught** in 1921 at the **Rashtrapati Bhavan** (then known as the Viceroy's House).
 
• This body consisted of **108 members**, including rulers of princely states and their representatives.
 
• The Chamber was a purely advisory body and had no legislative powers, functioning as a forum for princes to **exchange ideas and communicate with the British Government.**
 
• It was a part of the British Government's attempt to **control and manage** the princely states effectively.
 
• The Chamber ceased to exist after **India’s independence in 1947** when princely states were integrated into the Indian Union.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Council**__

 __
 
• The **Indian Council**, also known as the **Council of India**, was established under the **Government of India Act 1858** to assist the Secretary of State for India.
 
• It was not a deliberative body for princes but instead an advisory body for the administration of British India.
 
• The members of the Indian Council were based in **London** and were responsible for advising on policy matters.
 
 
 
• **Imperial Assembly**__
 __
 
• The term **Imperial Assembly** does not refer to any specific institution in the context of British India.
 
• It may appear to suggest a legislative body, but such an assembly did not exist under this name during British rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Royal Consultation Board**__
 
 
• The **Royal Consultation Board** is not a historically recognized institution under British rule in India.
 
• It does not relate to the Chamber of Princes or any similar body.
